metadata.title: Bilinear ergodic Hilbert variation for commuting transformations as a consequence of annular triangular variation
metadata.description: We give an explicit restriction and transference consequence of OpenAI's full annular variation theorem for the triangular Hilbert transform, manuscript dated October 5, 2026, at source commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a. For arbitrary commuting invertible probability-preserving transformations S,T and complex f,g in L3, the symmetric sums H_N=sum_(0<|n|<=N) f(S^n x)g(T^n x)/n, with H_0=0, satisfy a pointwise r-variation estimate in L^(3/2) for every r>2. They have a bounded maximum and converge almost everywhere and in L^(3/2), with maximal-tail convergence in that norm. The proof uses fixed positive-area cell boxes, half-integer radial endpoints, an explicitly summable O(k^-2) signed kernel error, and finite-menu finite-window Calderon transference. The continuous analytic breakthrough is inherited and credited; this note supplies its discrete restriction and ergodic consequence. Classical transference and its modern predecessors are credited, and no first-priority or independent triangular-Hilbert breakthrough claim is made. Scope remains L3 inputs, symmetric odd truncations, commuting transformations and r>2; there is no r=2, noncommuting or one-sided Cesaro claim. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. Automated adversarial audits are not human peer review or formal certification. The relevant Lean artifacts concern an older maximal theorem and do not formally verify full annular variation or this note. This preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing at publication.
